title: The Future of CPO May Be a Glass Integration Platform - Semiwiki
gist: Co-packaged optics is usually framed as moving the optical engine closer to the switch ASIC or XPU, but shortening electrical reach just relocates the bottleneck into the package — into substrate geometry, EIC/PIC integration, optical alignment and assembly yield. The argued conclusion is that glass, if through-glass vias, fine RDL and a supplier ecosystem mature, could become a large-area integration plane that participates in both electrical and optical routing rather than merely replacing organic substrates or silicon interposers.

insights.claim: Moving optical conversion closer to compute does not remove the physical constraint behind co-packaged optics; it relocates it into optical alignment sensitivity, thermal exposure, mechanical sensitivity and assembly repeatability inside the package.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Reframes CPO investment away from optical-engine makers and toward substrate, assembly and test suppliers who inherit the new constraint.
insights.quote: A physical bottleneck rarely disappears; it changes coordinates across the system.

insights.claim: Co-packaged optics should be understood as an integration-platform problem rather than an optical-engine problem, which changes which vendors capture the value.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Value-chain call: platform/substrate suppliers over point-solution photonics vendors.
insights.locator: That is why CPO cannot ultimately be understood

insights.claim: The package has crossed from supporting the system to defining which system can physically be built, making the substrate underneath a strategic rather than commodity layer.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: If true, substrate suppliers gain architectural veto power and pricing leverage in AI package BOMs.
insights.quote: The package is no longer merely supporting the system. It is defining what system can be built.
insights.locator: This connects directly to a broader thesis

insights.claim: Glass offers dimensional stability, low-loss high-frequency electrical routing, a smooth surface for fine redistribution structures and an engineerable coefficient of thermal expansion — a combination that matters more once optics enter the package.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: The specific property list to test against any glass-substrate vendor's claims.

insights.claim: Unlike a silicon interposer constrained by wafer geometry and economics, glass permits considerably larger integration dimensions, which is the property that matters as AI packages grow.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Large-area scaling is the structural argument for glass over interposers as package sizes outgrow reticle and wafer limits.
insights.locator: And unlike a conventional silicon interposer

insights.claim: Dimensional stability stops being a mere mechanical property and becomes an architectural capability once fiber attachment, couplers, waveguides and PIC placement are inside the package, because optical interfaces tolerate far less variation than electrical routing.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Explains why optics adoption, not electrical performance, is what finally pulls glass into production.
insights.quote: Electrical routing can tolerate certain variations that an optical interface may not.

insights.claim: Future glass structures could carry lateral electrical redistribution, vertical through-glass-via connectivity and eventually optical structures in the substrate itself, so the substrate would participate in the optical system rather than merely connect the optical engine to the ASIC.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: The blue-sky upside case for glass — optical routing in-substrate would collapse a whole layer of components.

themes.theme: Distributed optics changes the scaling problem

insights.claim: Today's CPO picture of one large switch ASIC surrounded by a handful of optical engines may not be the final architecture; as bandwidth density rises, optical functionality could become distributed across many smaller electronic and photonic functions around compute.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: If optics fragments into many small functions, per-unit optical-engine economics deteriorate while integration-platform economics improve.
insights.locator: Much of today's CPO discussion still assumes

insights.claim: A mature glass platform would need to supply large integration area, fine electrical redistribution, stable geometry, vertical connectivity and eventually optical routing simultaneously — making it an integration plane rather than a substrate material swap.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A five-item checklist for judging whether any announced glass program is strategic or incremental.

themes.theme: TGV and manufacturability as the real gate

insights.claim: The through-glass via is a critical gating technology whose difficulties are via geometry, glass damage, metallization, copper filling, interface adhesion, residual stress, cracking and long-term reliability, and these worsen as vias shrink and counts rise.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: TGV yield is the single technical milestone to track before glass becomes investable at scale.
insights.locator: TGV Is One of the Critical Gates

insights.claim: Glass should be evaluated on whether glass processing, TGV, fine RDL, assembly and reliability can mature into a repeatable manufacturing ecosystem, not on a material-property table.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Guards against being sold on datasheet properties; demand process-integration and yield evidence instead.
insights.locator: This is why the glass opportunity should not be evaluated

insights.claim: Excellent demonstrated optical performance from a PIC, high bandwidth from an optical engine, or superb electrical loss from a glass substrate individually establish nothing about a scalable product, because the system must still survive assembly, thermal cycling, mechanical stress, alignment, test, qualification and production yield.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A discipline for reading CPO press releases: component demos are not product evidence.
insights.quote: The optical function is not the product.
insights.locator: The Optical Function Is Not the Product

insights.claim: Glass is not a superior thermal material and does not inherently provide the heat-spreading capability of materials chosen for high thermal conductivity, so the thermal path must still be deliberately engineered through the full package.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Corrects a common bull-case error; glass adoption does not reduce demand for dedicated thermal solutions.
insights.quote: Glass should not automatically be described as a superior thermal material.
insights.locator: Glass Is Not Automatically a Thermal Solution

insights.claim: Glass-based integration requires compatible materials, process equipment, TGV manufacturing, fine-line redistribution, assembly methods, known-good-die strategies, inspection, qualification methods and multiple manufacturing sources before it can scale — an ecosystem that will take time to mature.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Multi-sourcing and inspection capability are the practical gating items; single-supplier glass programs stay niche.
insights.locator: Glass-based integration will require compatible materials

insights.claim: The recurring semiconductor pattern is that the first demonstration proves possibility, manufacturing proves repeatability, and the ecosystem determines scale — so the milestone that matters is when designers can choose glass without every program becoming a custom research project.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A staged adoption model for timing entry into any new packaging material, glass included.
insights.quote:
The first demonstration proves possibility.
Manufacturing proves repeatability.
The ecosystem determines scale.
insights.locator: The Ecosystem May Matter More Than the First Demonstration

insights.claim: The consequential question is not whether glass replaces organic substrates or silicon interposers, but whether it can become a scalable physical integration plane for many electronic and photonic functions around compute.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Substitution framing understates the TAM; platform framing implies glass could absorb functions from several adjacent component categories.
